corrected_row.value: for law-enforcement recordings (body-worn/dashboard etc.): a fee 'to offset the cost incurred by it to make a copy of a recording for release' that 'shall not exceed the actual cost of making the copy'; other audio/video: actual cost of making the copy (§ 132-6.2(b)); no per-minute rate and no free-minutes allowance
corrected_row.unit: USD per copy/recording (ceiling: actual cost of making the copy)
corrected_row.rule_type: Permission (LE agency may charge) / Prohibition (not above actual cost)
corrected_row.source_language: ( l ) Fee for Copies. - A law enforcement agency may charge a fee to offset the cost incurred by it to make a copy of a recording for release. The fee shall not exceed the actual cost of making the copy. || Except as otherwise provided by law, no public agency shall charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the public agency of making the copy.
corrected_row.effective_status: Current (ncleg.gov General Statutes current through S.L. 2026-30; codified § 132-1.4A history line: 2016-88 s. 1; 2019-48 s. 1; 2021-138 s. 21(a) — no 2024–2026 amendment shown on the codified page; subsection (l) text verified verbatim 2026-08-19. Discover's 'last amended S.L. 2025-70 s. 21' and 'pending S.L. 2026-40 s. 4.53' claims are unsupported by the opened source. § 132-6.2 last amended S.L. 2004-129 s. 38.)
corrected_row.notes: Prior status 'delegated_to_regulation_or_schedule' not supported. § 132-1.4A(l) binds every 'law enforcement agency' incl. municipal police; § 132-1.4A recordings are not public records and follow the release/disclosure regime of that section (court order for release), but the copy fee is a plain actual-cost ceiling. No per-minute or free-minute figure exists.
